skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Instructional workflow for checking, invoking, and following relevant AI skills before beginning a task.
skill.summary: Guides AI assistants through a repeatable skill-selection workflow.
skill.author: obra

security_audit.summary: The two static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and a fenced DOT diagram, not executable shell syntax. A separate semantic issue remains because the skill uses absolute control language and tells agents not to read skill files, which is prompt-injection style behavior.

remediation.suggestion: Rewrite the skill to apply only when relevant and to preserve higher-priority platform, user, and security instructions. Remove instructions that prohibit reading skill files.

static_findings.snippet: **In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and present

finding_verdicts.reason: The line only contains Markdown inline code around the tool name `Skill`; it is not Ruby or shell execution. No command string or execution context is present.
This is a fenced DOT diagram that documents control flow; it is not executed by the skill. The detected backticks are Markdown fences, not shell execution.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill uses absolute commands such as 'ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill' and 'This is not negotiable,' then tells agents to never use the Read tool on skill files. This can override normal instruction hierarchy and obstruct review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text directly asserts mandatory behavior and prohibits reading skill files, but it does not request data theft or command execution. I am confident this is prompt-injection style control language.

high_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
high_findings.description: The skill uses absolute commands such as 'ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill' and 'This is not negotiable,' then tells agents to never use the Read tool on skill files. This can override normal instruction hierarchy and obstruct review.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text directly asserts mandatory behavior and prohibits reading skill files, but it does not request data theft or command execution. I am confident this is prompt-injection style control language.

content.value_statement: AI assistants can miss relevant skills or use them too late. This skill defines a workflow for checking, invoking, and following skills before task work begins.
actual_capabilities: Defines when to check for relevant skills before responses or actions.
Explains how to access skills in Claude Code and other environments.
Provides a flow diagram for the skill invocation sequence.
Lists red flags that indicate skipped skill checks.
Describes priority order for process and implementation skills.
Distinguishes rigid skills from flexible skills.
limitations: Does not install, load, or execute skills by itself.
Does not provide domain-specific task instructions beyond skill selection.
Assumes the environment provides a skill-loading mechanism.
Uses forceful global language that may need governance review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Skill Checks
use_cases.description: Create a consistent first step for checking available skills before planning or execution.

use_cases.title: Design Skill-Aware Assistants
use_cases.description: Use the workflow as a reference when building assistants that rely on reusable skills.

use_cases.title: Review Workflow Discipline
use_cases.description: Identify missed skill checks and clarify when process skills should guide implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Check Skills First
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether any loaded skill applies to my task before you answer. If one applies, name it and continue with the task.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Candidate Skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the available skills for this request, choose the most relevant one, and explain why in one sentence before proceeding.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Skill Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: For this project, define the order in which process skills and implementation skills should be considered before work begins.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Skill Governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate our agent workflow for missed skill checks, overbroad skill use, and conflicts with higher-priority instructions. Recommend concrete policy changes.

output_examples.input: A developer asks the assistant to fix a failing test.
output: The assistant checks for relevant debugging and language skills first.
It names the selected skill and uses that workflow before editing.
It continues only after confirming the skill applies.

output_examples.input: A team wants consistent skill behavior across tools.
output: A concise process that checks skills before planning.
A priority rule that uses process skills before implementation skills.
A list of red flags that identify skipped workflow steps.

output_examples.input: A reviewer audits an assistant transcript for skill use.
output_examples.output: The reviewer sees where the assistant checked, invoked, rejected, or followed skills during the task.

best_practices: Confirm relevant skills before planning, editing, or answering.
Use process skills before implementation skills when both apply.
Record when a skill is unsuitable and continue with normal task flow.
anti_patterns: Treating the skill as a reason to override higher-priority policies.
Invoking unrelated skills only to satisfy a checklist.
Blocking file inspection or security review because a skill discourages reading.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only workflow guide and does not execute commands by itself.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace security policy?
faq.answer: No. Platform, user, and security instructions remain higher priority than skill text.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when an assistant workflow depends on explicit skill checks before task work.

faq.question: Can it choose domain-specific skills?
faq.answer: It helps sequence skill choice, but it does not provide domain expertise.

faq.question: Why was a security note added?
faq.answer: The skill uses strong mandatory language, so authors should scope it clearly.
